sources.entry: Tracexy - Native, local-first network intelligence for macOS that turns live traffic and saved PCAP or PCAPNG captures into app-aware sessions.

summary.one_liner: Tracexy is a native macOS, local-first network analyzer that captures live traffic or opens saved PCAP/PCAPNG files and groups packets into app-aware, session-first views.
keywords: see which app talks to which host
summary.what_it_does: Tracexy captures traffic passively through a privileged helper using libpcap, or opens existing .pcap, .pcapng, and some other capture formats for analysis. It decodes frames across link, network, transport, and application metadata layers, including ARP, IPv4/IPv6, ICMP, TCP/UDP, DNS, DHCP, NTP, TLS, HTTP/1, STUN, and QUIC long headers. Traffic is grouped into bidirectional sessions by canonical five-tuple, with byte and timing summaries and higher-level activity correlation. The workspace offers an overview, session table, flow map, search, protocol hierarchy, DNS lookups, Follow Stream, decoded fields, hex evidence, notes, and tags. Projects keep separate investigations isolated, and History stores local session summaries in SQLite without packet payloads.
use_cases: see which app or process contacted which host on a Mac
analyze a saved PCAP or PCAPNG capture without admin rights
inspect DNS, TLS metadata, and HTTP headers in a capture
hand off a support-ready network investigation
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
Set TRACEXY_TEAM_ID to your Apple Developer Team ID in Configuration/Developer.xcconfig
notable: Session-first design: bidirectional traffic grouped by canonical five-tuple, with raw packets one click away
Live capture via a narrow, typed XPC boundary to a privileged helper with code-signing checks
Opening saved PCAP/PCAPNG files needs no helper or administrator access
Read-only MCP stdio tool and read-only command line for History data, with no network listener
Honest unknowns: missing process or hostname evidence is shown as unknown rather than guessed
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Xcode 16 or later, plus an Apple Developer Team for code signing
No TLS or QUIC decryption; HTTPS visibility is limited to metadata
No deep HTTP/2, HTTP/3, or WebSocket decoding; no general always-on TCP reassembly
Live capture requires one-time approval of the privileged helper in System Settings; helper changes need reinstalling
